page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-c32g1.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on the Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz, supported by 376 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by two discrete NVIDIA A10 GPUs supplying 48 GB of total video memory across both cards. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps, while no local disk storage is bundled, necessitating external block storage for operating systems and persistence.

The compute and memory allocation establishes a ratio of roughly 5.88 GB per vCPU, balancing multi-core processing with sufficient memory overhead for large execution states. The dual NVIDIA A10 accelerator configuration supplies targeted graphic and matrix compute capacity. Without integrated ephemeral NVMe disks, data retrieval speeds depend directly on external storage attachments, making the 32 Gbps networking interface vital for maintaining pipeline throughput during large tensor or dataset ingest.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dual A10 configuration delivers high multi-GPU density and significant host compute capacity without escalating into higher-cost specialized training accelerator classes. This setup suits mid-scale parallel operations where enterprise AI training chips would be underutilized. Primary workload fits include deep learning inference serving, video transcode acceleration, 3D graphics virtualization, cloud workstation hosting, and high-concurrency scientific simulation workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-c32g1.16xlarge is a compute-optimized, GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor. It integrates 64 dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B vCPUs clocked at 2.9 GHz with 376 GB of system memory, providing approximately 5.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA A10 GPUs offering a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. The instance features a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for high-throughput data transfers, but includes no local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent data. This architecture provides balanced resource density for parallel processing without the overhead of enterprise-grade training clusters. The configuration is appropriate for deep learning inference, cloud gaming, 3D graphics rendering, video transcode pipelines, and data-intensive compute tasks requiring dedicated multi-GPU acceleration alongside high CPU core counts.
